album: Cookin' with the Miles Davis Quintet
label: Prestige
rationale: Cookin' is the first-released of the four LPs cut from the Miles Davis Quintet's fabled Prestige sessions, and the one that documents the First Great Quintet's live book in the studio: 'the first of the four albums derived from... the concept being that the band would document its vast live-performance catalog in a studio environment' [S2] (obs). Ira Gitler's original liner notes call them 'the group - the best small combo active in modern jazz' and quote Prestige's Bob Weinstock calling them 'the Louis Armstrong Hot Five of the modern era' [S3,S8] (obs). Lineage: the canon already holds the set's Relaxin' (1958) and the Columbia records that follow it; Cookin' is the missing first panel of the Prestige quintet - Davis, Coltrane, Garland, Chambers, Philly Joe Jones - the band Coltrane left for Giant Steps [S1,S2] (obs). Consensus across independent listing traditions: Wikipedia's review box records AllMusic 4.5/5, the Penguin Guide to Jazz 4/5, the Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 5/5, The Encyclopedia of Popular Music 4/5, All About Jazz 4/5, Disc 5/5 and Music Box 5/5 [S1] (obs). Session gravity is high: two marathon 1956 dates produced twenty-six master takes and four albums, repertory called on the stand rather than rehearsed for the date [S3,S4] (obs). It still plays: 'Tune Up/When Lights Are Low' is plainly a highlight of the quintet's whole tenure - 'all the elements converge upon this fundamentally swinging medley' (Lindsay Planer, AllMusic) [S2] (obs). Style note: filed hard-bop, matching the canon's filing of its sibling Relaxin' (1958); AllMusic tags it Bop/Hard Bop/Cool/Post-Bop [S2] (obs).

cover_art.notes: Release-group front; image matches the front cover AllMusic serves for the album. LP cover design Reid Miles, illustration Phil Hays [S1,S3].

personnel_record.notes: Single session. One date, October 26, 1956, Van Gelder Studio, Hackensack, NJ - all four LP sides come from masters 1002-1006 of that date [S4]. Wikipedia's prose says 'two sessions on May 11 and October 26, 1956, resulted in four albums' [S1]; the second (May 11) session is real but supplied Relaxin', Workin' and Steamin' material only - jazzdisco assigns none of its masters 888-901 to PRLP 7094 [S4], and both AllMusic and the LP's own liner notes give October 26, 1956 as the recording date [S2,S3]. Session durations differ between the LP liner-note print (5:59 / 9:59 / 4:24 / 13:08) [S3] and Wikipedia's listing (6:04 / 10:23 / 4:26 / 13:09) [S1]; Wikipedia's figures are recorded here. Side assignment A/A/B/B follows the LP track order and the RateYourMusic credit line for PRLP 7094 (Miles Davis 'composer A2, B2'); Wikipedia and AllMusic print a single sequential listing without sides.

ballot.album: Miles Davis — Cookin' with the Miles Davis Quintet (1957)
ballot.case_for: The album has broad critical support, including 4/5 from the Penguin Guide, 5/5 from the Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide, and 4.5/5 from AllMusic [S1]. It is the first-released document of the First Great Quintet’s working repertoire, with Davis, Coltrane, Garland, Chambers, and Philly Joe Jones captured at Van Gelder’s studio [S2, S3, S4]. The canon already holds its sibling Relaxin’, and Cookin’ adds distinctive performances including “My Funny Valentine” and the “Tune Up / When Lights Are Low” medley, which AllMusic’s Lindsay Planer calls a highlight of the quintet’s tenure [S2].
ballot.case_against: Cookin’ belongs to a batch of four Prestige albums assembled from marathon sessions, and Relaxin’ already represents this lineup and much of the same musical setting; a selective canon could reasonably decide that one sibling is enough. The dossier establishes Cookin’s distinct tracks and first-release status, but offers limited comparative critical analysis showing why this album is indispensable beyond those distinctions.
ballot.disagreement: Both references judge the album consensus_core, but differ on urgency and the weight of sibling-album redundancy: one calls it must_have and sees Relaxin’’s inclusion as making the omission conspicuous, while the other assigns strong priority and argues that Relaxin’ and ’Round About Midnight may already establish this lineup’s sound.
ballot.recommendation: John should treat Cookin’ as a strong core addition, while deciding whether its distinct repertoire and first-release role justify including another Prestige-session sibling.
